rv.q: Lim and her cast made it come alive for me again.
By the time it all ends in a virtual apocalypse of bubbles it’s safe to say that you will have been charmed.
Emily Lim’s take is frivolous, folksy and fun – and family-friendly, too.
Yet, for all the admirable industry and invention of Emily Lim’s production, at times I felt as if I’d been trapped in Butlin’s rather than spirited away to an enchanted forest outside Athens.
And this one is a glorious riot of colour and confusion.
It’s a Dream that’s very much in the Globe’s tradition of crowd-pleasing entertainment, filled with music, laughter, and appropriately absurd audience participation.
It’s just one of a number of ingenious little twists that make this a genuinely joyous, energetic and celebratory interpretation.
This version of Dream is something close to a folk musical, with original songs by Jim Fortune.
Lim’s production is bright and big on spectacle, making it brilliantly accessible to new audiences both young and old.

cn.t: Emily Lim's joyously frivolous production wins praise for its colorful, participatory approach and folk-inflected energy, though some find it lacks nuance. Critics celebrate the playful, audience-engaging spectacle as light summer fun.
